subject: Intermittent tail latency from customer edge — request for SLA exception
participants_external: michael@veloxsystems.com (Michael Chung, Velox Head of Platform)
messages:
From: ops@veloxsystems.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: [Velox] Intermittent 95th/99th latency spikes from our on-prem edge

Sergio / Naomi —

We surfaced recurring tail latency on our private deployment (VPC-peered colo) over the last 36 hours. The pattern is bursts every 2–6 hours that spike 95th/99th request latency into the 800–1200ms range for short windows (30–90s). Overall throughput and success rate are fine; it looks like something at our edge (NAT timeout + tcp retransmit) since traces show uneven RTT to the Redwoods fronting layer.

We attached a small set of packet captures and an edge trace slice (edge-trace-20280718.zip). Can we get confirmation this behavior would be considered a customer-controlled network tail for SLA attribution? Velox needs an operational carve-out on latency attribution while we troubleshoot the router firmware with our colo.

Next steps from our side: we can open a support ticket with the colo and share serials. From Redwood, can you propose temporary language that excludes short, customer-internal network congestion from latency SLO calculations?

Thanks —
Michael Chung
Head of Platform, Velox Systems
ops@veloxsystems.com

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: ops@veloxsystems.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Velox] Intermittent 95th/99th latency spikes from our on-prem edge

Michael —

Thanks for the packet captures and the trace. We took a preliminary look; the timing and the retransmit signatures do match an upstream NAT/device queuing event on your side. We agree in principle that short-duration customer-edge congestion should be excluded from Redwood’s latency SLO attribution if the evidence clearly shows the root cause lies outside the Redwood datapath.

Operationally, here’s what we need to proceed quickly:
- A 24h contiguous tranche of request-level traces showing the spikes (we have a 2h slice now).
- BGP/peering logs or colo ticket numbers showing any maintenance around the windows.
- Confirmation of the edge device model and current firmware (some NAT implementations have very low conn-tracking table defaults).

Kimberly (legal) and Naomi (Product) are looped for the wording and evidence thresholds. I’ll draft proposed carve-out language we can fast-track on a mutual action plan. If you’re open to a short temporary appendix (30/60-day trial), that will let us exclude verified customer-edge short tails while you remediate.

I’ve asked Product for a recommended evidence format so we minimize back-and-forth.

— Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: ops@veloxsystems.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Velox] Intermittent 95th/99th latency spikes from our on-prem edge

Sergio / Michael —

High level: Legal is sympathetic to a narrowly scoped operational attribution appendix. Key asks from our side to keep risk bounded:
- Timebox the exception (proposed 60 days) with an automatic expiry unless extended by mutual written agreement.
- Define a clear evidence bundle (traces, colo ticket id, device firmware, and a short CRC/sha of the trace artifact) and a single-window acceptance test.
- Limit the exclusion to latency SLO attribution only — not availability, not data integrity, not security.
- Include a clause that allows Redwood to re-evaluate if similar recurrence exceeds a set frequency (e.g., more than 3 events in 30 days).

I’ll review the draft language once Sergio shares. We should avoid open-ended carve-outs that could erode the SLO promise to other customers.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, ops@veloxsystems.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Velox] Intermittent 95th/99th latency spikes from our on-prem edge

Michael / team —

Product ran the trace through our diagnostics. Notes:
- The Redwood fronting tier sees steady upstream response times except during the spikes; the client RTT to our ingress jumps 3–5x during windows consistent with your captures.
- Because your deployment uses a private VPC-peering topology via an on-prem gateway, the KV cache and batching behavior is still intact; this is purely network-induced tail.

Suggested evidence format from Product:
1) A 24h contiguous trace capture in our .rtlog format (we can ingest the ZIP you sent; please include a short checksum).
2) Colo ticket ID or maintenance window that overlaps the spike times.
3) A short control test: 10 sequential requests from a pinned service at 5s intervals executed during a non-spike window to show baseline.

I’m attaching a draft Operational Attribution Appendix ("draft-sla-exception-velox.docx") with proposed thresholds and acceptance tests. If Velox can provide the 24h trace and a short control test, Product can validate and we can move to a 60-day exception appendix effective upon sign-off. During the exception, Redwood will continue to measure but will exclude verified customer-edge spikes from the 95th/99th latency SLO calculus.

Two practical notes:
- We will not apply the carve-out retroactively beyond the acceptance window.
- If spikes become frequent (more than 3 in a rolling 30d), we’ll pause the appendix and require a joint remediation plan.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Product — Operations, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Michael —

Thanks for the quick collaboration. We reviewed and updated the draft appendix attached (draft-sla-exception-velox.docx). Summary of the agreed flow:
- Velox provides a 24-hour contiguous trace capture + colo ticket ID + device firmware info and checksum.
- Product validates within 48 hours. If validated, both parties execute the 60-day Operational Attribution Appendix (appendix excludes verified customer-edge spikes from 95th/99th latency SLO attribution only).
- During the appendix window, Redwood will continue to highlight events but exclude validated spikes from rolling SLO calculations; repeated frequency >3/30d triggers re-evaluation.

Please confirm you will upload the 24h capture to the shared Drive link by EOD Monday 2028-07-23. Once we have that, Legal will generate a short signature page and we can fast-track execution.

Attachments: draft-sla-exception-velox.docx (proposed appendix)
Other artifacts you sent: edge-trace-20280718.zip

If any of the requirements are problematic, let me know and we’ll adjust. Appreciate the rapid triage — we want to keep Velox in a protected SLA posture without creating a broad precedent.

— Sergio
